note: One narrow idea per Short. Public-domain book; hooks and examples in our own modern words.

chapters.title: Part 1: See people as they are

episodes.title: How people are vs how they should be
episodes.hook: If you only see people as they should be, you'll get eaten alive.
episodes.angle: Plan for how people actually act, not how they ought to. Example: the trusting roommate who never puts names on his food.

episodes.title: Feared or loved?
episodes.hook: Is it better to be loved or feared? The answer is uncomfortable.
episodes.angle: Love can be broken when it's convenient; fear of consequences holds. But never be hated. Example: two teachers, the pushover and the strict-but-fair one.

episodes.title: Never be hated
episodes.hook: Being feared is a tool. Being hated is a death sentence.
episodes.angle: You can be strict without taking what people value. Example: a manager who enforces deadlines but never steals credit.

episodes.title: Gratitude runs out
episodes.hook: Don't build your plans on other people's gratitude.
episodes.angle: People forget favours when interests change. Example: the friend you helped move who's busy when you need help.

episodes.title: Everyone sees, few touch
episodes.hook: Everyone sees what you seem to be. Few know what you are.
episodes.angle: Most judge by appearance, so manage how you come across. Example: the person who looks prepared in the meeting versus the one who actually is.

episodes.title: Generosity can ruin you
episodes.hook: Being too generous makes people hate you later.
episodes.angle: Lavish giving can't last, and when it stops people feel robbed. Example: the boss who throws a huge party, then cuts bonuses.

episodes.title: Do the hard part at once
episodes.hook: Bad news? Deliver it all at once. Good news? Give it drop by drop.
episodes.angle: Harm done all at once is forgotten faster; benefits given slowly are savoured. Example: a coach who makes all the tough roster cuts on day one.

episodes.title: Avoid flatterers
episodes.hook: The people who agree with everything you say are the most dangerous.
episodes.angle: Surround yourself with honest advisers, and ask them only when you want to know. Example: an artist whose friends call every song a hit.

episodes.title: Luck is half
episodes.hook: Luck controls half your life. The other half is yours to build.
episodes.angle: Fortune is like a river; build dams in calm weather. Example: saving money while things are good instead of after you lose the job.

episodes.title: Prepare in calm times
episodes.hook: The time to prepare for a storm is when the sun is out.
episodes.angle: Most people only act once the crisis hits. Example: learning to code before your job gets automated.

episodes.title: Bold beats careful
episodes.angle: Fortune favours those who move decisively. Example: the shy guy who asks first and the careful one who waited too long.

episodes.title: Borrowed armor
episodes.hook: Other people's armor will either be too big or crush you.
episodes.angle: Depending on others' strength makes you weak. Example: a startup that relies on one big client.

episodes.title: Build your own foundation
episodes.hook: Whoever builds on other people's success falls with them.
episodes.angle: Self-made foundations are slow but stable. Example: two influencers, one who rides trends, one who builds skills.

episodes.title: The fox and the lion
episodes.hook: Be a fox to see the traps and a lion to scare the wolves.
episodes.angle: You need both cleverness and strength. Example: a negotiator who reads the room and holds firm.

episodes.title: Judge by results
episodes.hook: People judge you by results, not by your excuses.
episodes.angle: Outcomes outweigh intentions in other people's eyes. Example: the employee with the best reasons and the worst numbers.
